screenplay.text:
THE BREAD VAN

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written test screenplay for Panelwise (pronoun references).
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

         1     INT. NOMSA'S BAKERY - NIGHT                             1

               A narrow bakery with one big oven. Flour on every surface.
               Trays of bread rolls cool on a steel rack. A wall clock
               reads four o'clock.

               NOMSA (30s), flour up to her elbows, kneads dough on the
               counter. She works fast, without looking.

               THEO (9), in pyjamas and a school jersey, sleeps on a sack
               of flour in the corner. A small brown dog, BISCUIT, sleeps
               across his feet.

               The oven timer rings. Nomsa pulls out a tray of loaves and
               sets it on the rack.

                                     NOMSA
                               (under her breath)
                         Forty. Forty-one. Forty-two.

               She glances at Theo. He hasn't moved.

                                     NOMSA
                         Theo. Up. The van is late.

               Theo opens one eye. Biscuit opens both.

                                     THEO
                               (rubbing his eyes)
                         It's still dark.

                                     NOMSA
                         Bread doesn't care.

         2     EXT. BAKERY - NIGHT                                     2

               A quiet township street under one orange streetlight. A
               white delivery VAN with a dented door pulls up, its engine
               coughing.

               DANIEL (40s), a tall driver in a reflective vest, climbs
               out. He stretches until his back cracks.

               Nomsa comes out with a tray of loaves. She hands it to
               Daniel without a word.

                                     DANIEL
                         Good morning to you too.

                                     NOMSA
                         You are twenty minutes late.









                                                                       2.


                                     DANIEL
                         The van is twenty years old. It
                         does its best.

               He slides the tray into the back of the van. Nomsa goes back
               inside for the next one.

               Theo stumbles out with a bag of rolls held against his
               chest. Biscuit trots behind him.

                                     DANIEL
                         Is that the night shift?

                                     THEO
                         I'm the manager.

               Daniel laughs and takes the bag from him.

         3     INT. VAN - MOVING - DAWN                                3

               Daniel drives. Theo sits in the passenger seat with Biscuit
               on his lap. Behind them, the trays of bread rattle.

               The sky turns grey, then pink.

                                     THEO
                         Where do we go first?

                                     DANIEL
                         Auntie Betty. She pays in coins and
                         complaints.

                                     THEO
                         Mama says she's the best customer.

                                     DANIEL
                               (keeping his eyes on the
                               road)
                         Your mama is right about most
                         things.

         4     EXT. SPAZA SHOP - DAWN                                  4

               A small corner shop painted bright green. A hand-written
               sign in the window reads OPEN.

               AUNTIE BETTY (60s), in a woollen hat and slippers, waits on
               the step with her arms folded. A TAXI DRIVER leans on his
               taxi across the road, drinking tea from a flask.

               The van stops. Daniel jumps out with two trays.

                                     AUNTIE BETTY
                         Late.








                                                                       3.


                                     DANIEL
                         Auntie, the bread is still warm.
                         Feel it.

               She presses one loaf with a finger. She sniffs it. She nods.

                                     AUNTIE BETTY
                         Warm. Fine.

               She counts coins into his palm, one at a time.

               Theo climbs down from the van. Biscuit jumps down after him
               and runs straight at the taxi driver, tail wagging.

                                     THEO
                         Biscuit! Come back!

               The taxi driver crouches and scratches the dog behind the
               ears.

                                     AUNTIE BETTY
                               (to Theo)
                         Is that Nomsa's boy?

                                     THEO
                         Yes, Auntie.

               Auntie Betty takes a sweet from her pocket and puts it in
               his hand.

                                     AUNTIE BETTY
                         For the manager.

               Theo grins. Daniel shakes his head.

         5     INT. NOMSA'S BAKERY - DAY                               5

               Morning light fills the bakery. The rack is empty. Nomsa
               sits on the flour sack with a cup of tea, her eyes closed.

               The door opens. Theo runs in, Biscuit at his heels, and
               drops a fistful of coins on the counter.

                                     THEO
                         Auntie Betty paid. She said the
                         bread was fine.

                                     NOMSA
                               (opening her eyes)
                         Fine? That's the best review she
                         has ever given.

               Daniel leans in the doorway, keys in his hand.









                                                                       4.


                                     DANIEL
                         Same time tomorrow?

                                     NOMSA
                         Be on time tomorrow.

               He salutes and goes. The van coughs into life outside and
               pulls away.

               Nomsa pulls Theo onto her lap. He is already falling asleep.
               Biscuit curls up at her feet.

                                                            FADE OUT.
